matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely obliterated by nearly 30 points this week—and that's being generous since his roster played like it was punishing him for whatever war crimes he committed in the draft. Flamur showed up with an actual functioning team while Rob's lineup looked like he let his dog walk across the keyboard to set his starting lineup. At this point Rob should just start a new league called "How to Burn 29 Fucking Points in One Week" because that's the only thing he's consistently good at.

Rinor got within spitting distance of 100 points and still managed to choke away a W by 4.1—congratulations on assembling a roster so monumentally mid that you couldn't even clear the century mark to salvage the loss. You were close enough to taste victory and instead ate shit, which is basically your team's entire season in a nutshell. Arben didn't even need to play well; he just needed you to continue being the fantasy football equivalent of a participation trophy. Better luck next week, you absolute dunce.

Adam got absolutely worked this week, dropping 108.8 points and still eating a 12.7-point loss like he paid for the privilege. This is what happens when you trust your gut instead of literally any reputable source—your "gut" apparently has the forecasting abilities of a concussed squirrel. Nori didn't even need to break a sweat, just showed up and watched Adam's season slowly circle the drain while he grabbed the easy W. Better luck next week, champ, though at this rate "luck" might be your only play left.

Rilind got absolutely cock-punched this week, losing by a measly 5.9 points—which is basically fantasy football's way of saying "you were *this close* to not sucking." Ben rolled through with 83.6 points while Rilind limped across the finish line at 77.7, managing the rare feat of being simultaneously too incompetent to win and too pathetic to even lose spectacularly. That's not heartbreak, that's just the sound of a roster that quit before kickoff.

Veton got absolutely dick-slapped by 16 this week, and honestly, that's what happens when you field a roster that looked like it was assembled by someone playing fantasy football on their phone while taking a shit. 138 points? That's the kind of score that gets you laughed out of a league chat, not just a single matchup—Jetmir walked away feeling like he'd won the lottery while Veton's team played like it was actively trying to tank. Better luck next week, chief, because this wasn't unlucky—this was just sad.

Faton got absolutely obliterated 118-79.7, losing by nearly 40 points like he showed up to the draft drunk and forgot he was playing fantasy football. That's not a loss, that's a fucking massacre—his entire roster combined couldn't outscore Ilir's second-string garbage, and we're pretty sure his bench was actively rooting against him. Maybe next time don't treat your waiver wire like a charity donation center and actually field a competitive team.

matchups.preview: Arben's steamrolling through this league like he actually knows what he's doing, but Rob's about to remind everyone that 0-4 isn't a curse—it's a lifestyle choice. Rob's been making decisions all season like he's got money on his own team losing, and this week he's gonna get absolutely humbled by someone who remembered you're supposed to *start* your good players.

Flamur's sitting pretty at 4-0, but let's be real—that's the fantasy equivalent of catching a hot streak at a casino before the house takes back everything you won and your rent money. Nori's only one game back and hungry, while Flamur's roster is one injury away from looking like a waiver wire clearance sale. This is where the undefeated record gets exposed by someone with actual depth.

Rinor's been treading water at 2-2 with a roster that screams "I panic-drafted and haven't looked back," while Ben's somehow stumbled into the same record despite having actual talent on the bench—this week one of them finally remembers what a waiver wire is, and spoiler alert, it won't be Rinor. May the least incompetent team win, because both of you are playing like you forgot you're in a league with actual stakes.

Adam's hanging onto life support at 1-3 while Veton's already flatlined at 0-4, but don't let that fool you—this is a race to the bottom between two teams that've forgotten what a winning week looks like. Adam's been coasting on fumes and one lucky W, but facing Veton's historically incompetent roster this week is exactly the kind of "least bad" matchup that'll probably still come down to some waiver-wire scrub going off. Buckle up, because one of these dumpster fires is about to get slightly less smoky.

Rilind's limping in at 1-3 like a guy who thought he had a master plan but forgot to actually execute it—meanwhile Faton's sitting pretty at 2-2 with the kind of mediocre consistency that'll somehow still beat whatever dumpster fire Rilind's got rolling out there this week. This matchup's got "desperate team grasping at straws" energy all over it, and spoiler alert: those straws are made of wet paper and delusion.

Jetmir and Peter are about to get a masterclass in what actual competent fantasy football looks like when Ilir rolls through 3-1 while they're still sitting at .500 trying to figure out where it all went wrong. Family dinner's gonna be real quiet this year when Ilir's rubbing that win in their faces all season long, and they'll have nothing but excuses and a middle-of-the-pack record to show for it. Better start practicing your apologies now, because the Asllani household is about to have a clear hierarchy, and spoiler alert: you two aren't at the top.
